needs.text: Does the alleged conduct after 9 June 1952 fall within subletting, assignment, or other parting with possession of all or part of the shop under the fixed section 14(1)(b) ground?
What does the allowed record show about Duli Chand's retained legal possession or control versus Sri Bhagwan's exclusive possession and business use?
Was landlord written consent obtained or pleaded for any relevant parting, transfer, or subletting?
How do the competing son, adoption, and family-business assertions bear on whether Sri Bhagwan's occupation reflects parting with legal possession?
Do the supplied sub-tenancy notice or direct-tenancy provisions have any triggered role when the record says subletting did not arise but prior section 14(1)(b) eviction orders were entered?

objects.text: shop No. 361 (Old No. 467 25-A), Azadpur, G.T. Road, Delhi
M/s Aggarwal Hardware and Mills Stores
written landlord consent for parting with possession

facts.text: The landlord filed a section 14(1)(b) eviction petition concerning the shop and alleged that Duli Chand sublet or parted with possession after 9 June 1952 to M/s Hira Lal Sri Bhagwan without written consent.
facts.speaker: LANDLORD
unknown: court acceptance of alleged lack of written consent
facts.quote: the tenant-Duli Chand has sub:let or parted with the possession of the said shop after 9th day of June, 1952 to M/s Hira Lal Sri Bhagwan illegally and without the written consent of the landlord

facts.text: The tenant denied subletting or parting with possession and pleaded that possession of the shop remained with him.
facts.speaker: TENANT
facts.quote: there was no sub-letting or parting with the possession of the shop

facts.text: The tenant asserted that Sri Bhagwan was his son and that the business name M/s Hira Lal Sri Bhagwan commemorated the deceased relative Hira Lal.
facts.speaker: TENANT
facts.quote: Sri Bhagwan is the son of the tenant, and that the name of the business was given as M/s Hira Lal Sri Bhagwan in memory of the deceased relative Hira Lal

facts.text: The landlord replied that Sri Bhagwan, though Duli Chand's natural son, had been adopted by Hira Lal and had gone out of Duli Chand's family, and characterized the situation as subletting or parting with possession.
facts.speaker: LANDLORD
facts.quote: though Sri Bhagwan was the natural son of the tenant-Duli Chand, he had been given in adoption to Hira Lal

facts.text: The target court states that the question of subletting did not arise on the facts and circumstances presented.
facts.speaker: COURT
facts.quote: the question of subletting did not arise

facts.text: The target court records that the tenant never pleaded that he had obtained written landlord consent for parting with possession.
facts.speaker: COURT
unknown: whether any written consent existed outside the pleaded record
facts.quote: The tenant never pleaded that he had obtained any written consent from the landlord for parting with posses- sion.

facts.text: The target court frames the remaining consideration as whether the tenant parted with possession of the whole or part of the tenanted premises.
facts.speaker: COURT
facts.quote: The only question, therefore, for consideration in this case is as to whether the tenant had parted with pos- session of the whole or part of the tenanted premises.

facts.text: The Rent Controller held that the landlord had not proved that the tenant parted with possession of the shop.
facts.speaker: COURT
facts.quote: The learned Rent Controller held that the landlord had not proved parting with possession of the tenanted shop by the tenant.

facts.text: On the landlord's appeal, the Rent Control Tribunal held that the tenant had parted with legal possession and ordered eviction under section 14(1)(b).
facts.speaker: COURT
facts.quote: the Rent Control Tribunal held that the tenant had parted with the legal possession of the tenanted premises

facts.text: The High Court dismissed the tenant's second appeal and confirmed the Tribunal finding that the tenant had parted with possession of the shop.
facts.speaker: COURT
facts.quote: The second appeal filed by the tenant to the High Court was dismissed confirming the finding of the Rent Control Tribunal that the tenant had parted with possession of the tenanted shop.

facts.text: The Tribunal found, and the High Court accepted, that M/s Hira Lal Sri Bhagwan was Sri Bhagwan's sole proprietary concern.
facts.speaker: COURT
facts.stage: Tribunal findings accepted by High Court
facts.quote: the concern M/s Hira Lal Sri Bhagwan is the sole proprietary concern of Sri Bhagwan

facts.text: The Tribunal found, and the High Court accepted, that Duli Chand had no interest in Sri Bhagwan's business.
facts.speaker: COURT
facts.stage: Tribunal findings accepted by High Court
facts.quote: Duli Chand-tenant had no interest in the business

facts.text: The Tribunal found, and the High Court accepted, that Sri Bhagwan was in exclusive possession of the property.
facts.speaker: COURT
facts.stage: Tribunal findings accepted by High Court
facts.quote: Sri Bhagwan is in exclusive possession of the property

facts.text: The Tribunal/High Court findings recorded no plea of concurrent use by Duli Chand or licensee status for Sri Bhagwan, occasional presence of Duli Chand in the shop, and no retained control by Duli Chand.
facts.speaker: COURT
facts.stage: Tribunal findings accepted by High Court
facts.quote: there was no plea of concurrent user of the premises by the tenant nor there is any plea that Sri Bhagwan is a licensee

facts.text: Counsel for the tenant-appellant contended that Sri Bhagwan was not Hira Lal's adopted son and that allowing a son to conduct business did not establish parting with legal possession.
facts.speaker: TENANT
facts.quote: Sri Bhagwan was not the adopted son of Hira Lal and that by permitting the son to carry on business it could not be stated that he had 469 parted with the legal possession of the premises.

facts.text: Counsel for the tenant-appellant invoked a cited adoption rule requiring a formal giving-and-taking ceremony and asserted that evidence of a valid adoption was unavailable in this case.
facts.speaker: TENANT
unknown: legal effect on the fixed possession issue
facts.quote: such an evidence of a valid adoption is not available in this case.
